beats: slot 1 opens on the system working normally — the parts (people, apps, servers, places) and how one request or decision travels between them
slot 2 is the breaking point — the moment the flow overloads, leaks or fails, with the number that shows how bad it gets
slot 3 is the mechanism that fixes it — one part added or one rule changed, explained step by step as flows between the parts
slot 4 is the payoff — the same system under the same load, now holding, with the one idea worth remembering
title_patterns: how-it-works explainer ("How Apps Survive a Million Requests")
numbered concepts ("5 Ideas Behind Every App You Use")
breaking-point story ("Why One Slow Server Can Crash Everything")
story_structure.payoff_rule: the closing replays the system once more, now working, and lands one idea in a single sentence — never a summary list
story_structure.format_description: Visualcoders-style systems explainer: one glowing diagram per chapter on black, flows of requests/money/people moving between parts, badges, statement screens and side cards, every change fired on the spoken word. Brand name and colours come from each channel's own kit.

variation_rules: distinct system per video — the mechanism examined differs from every one in the channel's last 5 videos (enforced: the variation gate similarity + seed rotation)
no recycled example set against the last 5 videos (enforced: the variation gate similarity)
no repeated hook across the channel's last 5 videos (enforced: the variation gate similarity)
every number is concrete and attributable (a measured rate, a count, a date) — prose for the author and the review desk

changelog.note: the Living Diagram doc look in the glow style (owner: reusable for future channels) — same engine as money-flow-diagram (story_structure.doc_render = diagram, doc_presentation.style = glow); brand name/colours/voice come from each channel's kit; falls back to the storybook look on any failure (docs/templates/living-diagram.md)
